private-by-default.title: Private from the start: who sees what
private-by-default.summary: Only the people on the team see the plan. Money and private requests are visible only with access granted separately, person by person.
private-by-default.keywords: private confidential who sees access roles finance private requests contact details team

body.p1: An occasion is not visible to anyone outside its team. There are no public links to the plan, and a role says what each person can do, not everything they can see.

ul1.a: The plan (tasks, programme, suppliers, deliveries) — the whole team sees it, according to role.
ul1.b: Finance (“Budget”, “Shared costs”, supplier amounts) — only the owner and people with the “Finance” access.
ul1.c: Guests' “Private requests” — only the owner and people with the “Private requests” access.

body.note1: The budget, shared costs and private requests are not visible from any role apart from the owner. They are granted separately, to each person, from “Team and roles”. Not even a project manager gets them automatically.
body.h2: What does not leave the plan

ul2.a: Guests' contact details are seen only by the owner and the project manager.
ul2.b: Guests do not see the list of other guests. At the tables, each person sees only their own seat.
ul2.c: A supplier with a link sees only their own booking — no prices, guests or other suppliers.
ul2.d: A business you write to receives exactly what you see in the enquiry form and nothing else.
ul2.e: The “Gift estimator” is yours alone: what you work out there does not appear to other organisers, to guests, in exports or to assistants.

body.note2: Changing roles and access asks you to confirm again that it is you, and every change stays in the log of actions.

children-count-only.title: About children we keep only a count
children-count-only.summary: No names, no ages, no dates of birth. Everywhere in EventDesk children appear only as a number.
children-count-only.keywords: children count minors age name date of birth protection import reply

body.p1: When a household replies to the invitation, it says how many adults and how many children are coming. That is all. The guest list holds only the adults, by name; children appear as “+2 children”.

ul1.a: When adding a household: you list only the invited adults.
ul1.b: On import: columns with ages or dates of birth are left aside, and rows that seem to describe a child are skipped.
ul1.c: In the questions for guests: do not ask for details about children.
ul1.d: On the guest's link: if they type a child's name or age in a field, we ask them to remove it.
ul1.e: In private requests: the need itself is enough (“a gluten-free menu”), without the child's name or age.
ul1.f: At check-in: you record how many adults and how many children arrived.
ul1.g: For AI assistants and in exports: children appear only as a count.

body.note1: If you need a children's menu or a high chair, the number is enough for the supplier: “4 children's menus”.
body.p2: The rule is the same for every occasion and cannot be changed in settings.

facts-and-corrections.title: Facts stay facts: how to correct a payment or an arrival
facts-and-corrections.summary: What has already happened is not overwritten. It is corrected with a reason, and the old value stays in the history.
facts-and-corrections.keywords: correction correct fact payment arrival received quantity reason history mistake void
facts-and-corrections.where: Budget · Suppliers · Deliveries and returns · Check-in · Shared costs

body.p1: A plan changes all the time; a fact does not. If a payment was made, a delivery arrived or a household turned up, the record stays. If you made a mistake, you do not delete it — you correct it.

ul1.a: A paid expense — on its page, “Correct the payment”.
ul1.b: A supplier payment marked by mistake — “Correct the payment”, under “Payments”.
ul1.c: A received or returned quantity — “Correct the received quantity”, in “Deliveries and returns”.
ul1.e: A shared cost — “Void entry”; it stays in the list, marked “Voided”.

ol1.a: Press the correction button next to the record.
ol1.c: Type the reason, briefly (at least 3 characters).

body.note1: The correction keeps the old value, the new value, the reason, who made it and when. You see them under “Corrections” or “Correction history”.
body.note2: For the same reason a published briefing and a fixed final order are never edited: you publish or fix a new version, and the old one stays.

honest-directory.title: The business directory: the order is not for sale
honest-directory.summary: Every listing is checked by a moderator, and the order of results rotates daily. A paid placement shows position, never preference.
honest-directory.keywords: directory businesses order rotation featured paid placement no stars no reviews checked facts unclaimed

ul1.a: Every listing is checked by a moderator before it appears.
ul1.b: The order of results rotates daily. It is not for sale.
ul1.c: There are no stars, no scores and no customer opinions. Nobody can buy a better image.
ul1.d: A listing can show only two checked facts: registration with the trade register (ONRC) and insurance seen by a moderator.
ul1.e: Response statistics (how often and how quickly the business answers) appear only after ten answered enquiries, are calculated daily and cannot be bought.

body.p1: If a business pays for a position, the listing carries the label “Featured — paid placement”, written as visibly as the business name. The label says one thing only: that the position was paid for. It does not say the business is better and it does not change what you learn about it.
body.note1: For planners EventDesk is free. We take no commission on what you pay suppliers.
body.p2: A listing marked “Added by EventDesk — not claimed yet” comes from a public source, shown on its page. Its contact is shown as the business publishes it; EventDesk does not broker the contact.
body.p3: If you see something wrong or unlawful on a listing, use “Report” on its page.

report-content.title: Report illegal content or an unlawful listing
report-content.summary: Anyone can flag a problem. You do not need an account and you receive a reference for your report.
report-content.keywords: report illegal content unlawful listing abuse complaint reference moderator

ol1.a: Open the report form from “Contact and reporting” or from the “Report” link on a listing's page (the listing is then filled in already).
ol1.b: Choose what kind of problem it is.
ol1.c: Under “What is wrong”, say briefly what you saw and why you think it is illegal, in at least 10 characters.
ol1.e: Write down the reference shown. Keep it if you want to come back to the report.

body.p1: The report is read by an EventDesk moderator. The form's page tells you, step by step, what happens to it and points you to the moderation rules.
body.note1: You do not need an account to report.

ul1.a: You are the business in an unclaimed listing and want it removed or corrected: use “Ask for removal or a correction” on its page.
ul1.b: You have a problem with an invitation or an event: write to the host.
ul1.c: Something is not working in the app: check “Service status” under “Contact and reporting”.
